summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with psoriatic arthritis on chronic immunosuppression was admitted for an acute exacerbation of cervicogenic headache. The headache, consistent with prior flares, began in the occipital region and generalized, unresponsive to home morphine. He was treated in the ED with IV morphine and solumedrol, then transitioned to oral pain medications. Rheumatology recommended no steroid dose change. The pain service performed a bilateral greater occipital nerve block with bupivacaine and steroid, after which pain improved. He continued on prednisone, azathioprine, and Augmentin for an axillary abscess. Diabetes management included holding glyburide and continuing insulin. He was discharged home with stable pain, medication adjustments, and follow-up planned with pain and rheumatology clinics.
